claims.text: Real GDP increased at an annual rate of 1.6 percent in the first quarter of 2026, up from 0.5 percent in the fourth quarter of 2025.

citations.quotation: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 1.6 percent in the first quarter of 2026 (January, February, and March), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis. In the fourth quarter of 2025, real GDP increased 0.5 percent.

claims.text: The second estimate revised real GDP growth for Q1 2026 down 0.4 percentage point from the advance estimate of 2.0 percent, primarily reflecting downward revisions to investment and consumer spending.

citations.quotation: Real GDP was revised down 0.4 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting downward revisions to investment and consumer spending.

claims.text: The revision is a statistical update to the estimate, not a change in actual economic activity; the economy still grew faster in Q1 2026 than in Q4 2025 per the second estimate.

citations.quotation: Real GDP increased at an annual rate of 1.6 percent (0.4 percent at a quarterly rate1) in the first quarter, a downward revision of 0.4 percentage point from the previous estimate, primarily reflecting downward revisions to investment and consumer spending.

counterarguments.text: Real GDI grew only 0.9 percent in Q1 2026, below real GDP's 1.6 percent, suggesting the income-side measure shows weaker growth than the product-side GDP figure.

citations.quotation: 0.9 percent in the first quarter of 2026, compared with an increase of 1.6 percent in the fourth quarter of 2025. The average of real GDP and real GDI increased 1.3 percent

limitations: The revision (a change in the statistical estimate from 2.0 to 1.6 percent) should not be conflated with a slowdown in economic growth itself; no source text makes an explicit statement distinguishing the two beyond the revision explanation.
Source coverage is partial; the text is truncated mid-sentence regarding which components drove the acceleration versus Q4 2025.
Real GDI for the advance estimate is not provided ('…' in the table), so a full advance-vs-second comparison of GDI is unavailable.
Publication date (2026-05-28) is declared in source metadata and not independently verified.
